en: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dazhi of Baizhang Mountain in Hongzhou.

His name was Huaihai; he was a native of Changle in Fuzhou and belonged to the secular surname Wang. Having left the household life at the age of seven, he became thoroughly proficient in the three studies of the Buddhist canon.
At a time when Mazu Daichi was propagating his teachings in Jiangxi, the Master devoted himself to him with total sincerity and became his attendant, along with Xitang Zhizang and Nanquan Puyuan.
Quan Puyuan was one of those who entered the inner sanctum alongside [Baizhang]; at that time, these three great adepts stood out as preeminent figures.
While the Master was attending Mazu, they were walking along when a flock of wild ducks flew past. Mazu asked, "What is that? The Master replied, "Wild ducks. Mazu said:

“Where has he gone? The Master said, “He flew away. The Patriarch then turned his head and gave the Master’s nose a tug. In his agony, the Master let out a cry. The Patriarch said, “And yet you say he flew away? At these words, the Master attained realization. He returned to the attendants’ quarters and wept bitterly. A colleague asked him, “Are you thinking of your parents? The Master replied, “No. [The colleague] asked, “Then why are you crying? The Master said, “I am crying because I have lost my nose. The colleague said, “Your nose was here just a moment ago; where did it go? The Master said, “It flew away. The colleague said, “If that is so, why did you cry just now? The Master said, “I cried because I had not yet realized that my nose had flown away. The colleague said, “If that is so, why do you cry now? Someone asked, "Is it because you have been insulted? The Master said, "No. The person asked, "Then why are you weeping? The Master said, "My nostrils were pinched by the Great Master until the pain was unbearable.
A fellow practitioner asked, "What circumstance has arisen that you do not find harmonious? The Master said, "Go ask the Abbot yourself.
The fellow practitioner went to the Great Master and asked, "Attendant Hai, what circumstance has arisen that you do not find harmonious, such that you are weeping in your quarters?"
[The Master] said, "The Preceptor told me, 'The Great Master says that he understands; you should go ask him yourself.
When they returned to the quarters together, [the Master] said, "The Preceptor said, 'You understand; let me ask you myself. The Master then laughed heartily.
His companion asked, "Just now you were weeping; why are you laughing now? The Master replied, "Just now I was weeping; now..."
He laughed. His colleagues were bewildered. The next day, when Mazu ascended the hall and the assembly had just gathered, the Master stepped forward and rolled up the sitting mat.
Mazu immediately descended from his seat. The Master followed him to the abbot’s quarters. Mazu said, "I did not say a single word just now; why did you roll up the mat?
The Master replied, "Yesterday, I was grabbed by the nose by you, Master, until my head ached. Mazu said, "As for yesterday..."
“Hirō, where have you been applying your mind? The Master said, “Today my nose does not ache again. The Patriarch said, “You have thoroughly understood what happened yesterday.
The Master bowed and withdrew. (In one version, it says Mazū asked: “Where have you come from? Yesterday I had some business to attend to and was unable to accompany you for your study.”)
Mazu gave a shout. The Master then went out. Later, while standing in attendance during another visit, Mazu looked at the whisk in the corner of his rope bed.
The Master said, "Is it used as this, or apart from this? Mazu said, "When you open your two flaps of skin in the future, with what will you save people?"
The Master took up his whisk and held it upright. The Patriarch said, "Use this very thing, yet remain detached from its use. The Master hung the whisk back in its original place.
The Patriarch let out a thunderous shout, which left the Master deaf for three days. From that time on, his voice was like a rolling thunder.
Lay devotees invited him to the border of Xinwu in Hongzhou to reside at Mount Daxiong; because the mountain peaks and crags there were exceedingly steep and lofty, he took up residence there.

He was given the title Baizhang. Once he had settled there, before even a full year had passed, guests who had penetrated the mysteries of the profound Way arrived from all quarters like a swarm of deer;
among them, Guishan and Huangbo were the foremost.
When Huangbo arrived at the Master’s place, one day he took his leave, saying, “I wish to go and pay my respects to Mazu.
The Master said, “Mazu has already passed away. Huangbo asked, “I wonder what words or phrases Mazu left behind?
The Master then related the occasion of Huangbo’s second visit to Mazu when he held up his whisk, saying, “The Buddha-dharma is no small matter. At that time, I was nearly struck by Master Ma.”
With one shout, he left [Baizhang] with ringing in his ears for three days. When Huangbo heard this being recounted, he involuntarily stuck out his tongue.

The Master said, "In the future, will you not take up the lineage of Mazu? Huangbo replied, "Not so. Today, because of what you have related, I have been able to see the great function of Mazu’s spiritual power.
However, I do not yet know Mazu personally. If I were to succeed him, my descendants would lose their way in the future."

The Master said, "So it is, so it is. When one's insight is equal to that of the teacher, one has diminished the teacher’s virtue by half; only when one's insight surpasses that of the teacher is one fit to receive the transmission.
You possess a vision that greatly transcends your teacher. Later, Guishan asked Yangshan about the circumstances of Baizhang’s second visit to Mazu regarding the raising of the whisk:
"What was the intent of these two venerable elders? Yangshan replied, "This was to manifest the Great [Dharma]."

Regarding the function of the "great capacity" (*daji*) and the "great function" (*dayong*), Guishan said: "Among the eighty-four *kalyāṇamitras* produced by Mazu, how many attained the great capacity?
How many attained the great function? Yangshan replied: "Baizhang attained the great capacity; Huangbo attained the great function;
all the others were merely teachers who proclaimed the Way. Guishan said: "So it is, so it is."
One day Mazu asked the Master, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From behind the mountain.
Mazu said, "Did you encounter anyone there? The Master said, "I did not encounter anyone. Mazu said, "Why did you not encounter anyone?
The Master said, "If I had encountered anyone, I would have reported it to you, Reverend. Mazu said, "Where did you get this news? The Master said, "I..."
"Your fault," [the monk] said. Baizhang replied, "Rather, it is my own fault.
He then ascended the hall and said: "The numinous light shines alone, utterly transcending the sense organs and their objects. Its essence reveals the true permanence, unbound by words and letters.
The nature of mind is unstained; it is fundamentally perfected from the beginning. Simply leave behind delusive conditions, and you are the Buddha of Suchness."
A monk asked, "What is the extraordinary matter? The Master said, "Sitting alone on Mount Daxiong. The monk bowed; the Master then struck him.
Xitang asked the Master, "How will you instruct others in the future? The Master rolled and unrolled his hand twice. Xitang asked, "And how else? The Master tapped his head three times with his hand.
Mazu sent someone with a letter and three jars of sauce for the Master. The Master ordered them to be placed before the Dharma Hall and then ascended the hall.
As soon as the assembly had gathered, the Master pointed his staff at the jars of sauce and said, "If you can speak, I will not break these;
if you cannot speak, I shall break them. The assembly was speechless. The Master then broke the jars and returned to his quarters.
A monk entered the Dharma Hall weeping. The Master asked, "What are you doing? The monk replied, "Both my parents have passed away;
I ask the Master to select an auspicious day for their burial. The Master said, "Tomorrow, bury them all at once."

Question: "If one interprets the meaning based on the sutras, one is an enemy of the Buddhas of the three periods; if one deviates from a single word of the sutras, it is like the teaching of a demon—how is this so?
The Master said: "To cling rigidly to movement and stillness is to be an enemy of the Buddhas of the three periods; to seek something else apart from this is to be like the teaching of a demon."

On one occasion, after the Master had finished preaching the Dharma, the great assembly descended from the hall. He then called out to them, and as the assembly turned their heads, the Master asked, "What is this?
Later, upon returning from the communal labor of clearing the fields, the Master asked Acharya Yun: "Was it not difficult to clear the fields? Yun Ba replied, "The monks did it."
The Master said, "I fear it will trouble your practice. Baizhang said, "How would I dare decline such toil? The Master asked, "How many fields have you plowed?
Baizhang made the gesture of hoeing a field. The Master then shouted, and Baizhang covered his ears and went out.
The Master asked Huangbo, "Where have you come from? Huangbo replied, "I have come from picking mushrooms at the foot of the mountain.
The Master said, "There is a tiger cub at the foot of the mountain; did you see it? Huangbo then made a tiger's roar. The Master drew a hatchet from his waist and made a gesture as if to strike him.
Huangbo grabbed him and gave him a slap. That evening, the Master went up to the hall and said to the assembly, "At the foot of the mountain there was a tiger cub."
"You all, look well when entering or leaving. This old monk has just now personally suffered one mouthful.
Later, Mount Wei asked Yangshan, "How do you understand the story of Huangbo as a tiger? Yangshan said, "What about you, Master?
Mount Wei said, "At that time, Baizhang ought to have struck him dead with a single axe. Why did it come to this? Yangshan said, "Not so."
Guishan said, "How about you, my son? Yangshan replied, "Not only do I ride the tiger's head, but I also know how to grasp its tail.
Guishan said, "Ji, you have truly uttered words of the precipice."
Every day when the Master ascended the hall for teaching, there was always an old man who listened to the Dharma and would disperse along with the assembly. One day he did not leave.
The Master then asked, "Who is that person standing there? The old man replied, "In the past, during the time of Kāśyapa Buddha, I once lived on this mountain.
A student asked me, 'Does one who practices great cultivation still fall within the realm of cause and effect? To which I replied:"
"Not falling into cause and effect" resulted in his falling into the body of a wild fox. He now requests the Master to provide a turning phrase on his behalf. The Master said, "But ask.
The old man then asked, "Does a person of great cultivation still fall into cause and effect? The Master said, "He does not obscure cause and effect.
At these words, the old man attained great enlightenment. Taking his leave, he said to the Master, "I have now escaped the wild fox body."

A body was found dwelling behind the mountain; [the master] requested that it be cremated according to the rites for deceased monks. The Master ordered the *vinaya-dhara* (Rector) to strike the wooden mallet and announce to the assembly:
"After the midday meal, we shall all be invited to escort the deceased monk. The great assembly did not understand the details.

The Master led the multitude to the base of a cliff behind the mountain and, using his staff, pried out a dead fox. He then performed the cremation according to the Dharma. That evening, during the formal assembly (*sāṃghika*), the Master recounted the preceding circumstances.
Yellow Peak then asked, "An ancient fell into the body of a wild fox because he gave one wrong response. Today, how is it that you have not given a single wrong response?
The Master said, "Come closer; I will tell you. Yellow Peak stepped forward and struck the Master with his palm.
The Master clapped his hands and laughed, saying, "I thought the beard was red, but here is a red-bearded barbarian! At that time, Guishan was present.
While serving as the *dianzuo* (kitchen steward) under the assembly, Sima Tou-tuo raised the "Wild Fox" kōan and asked, "How would you respond, *dianzuo*?
The *dianzuo* struck the door panels three times with his hand. Sima said, "That is too crude. The *dianzuo* replied, "The Buddha-dharma is not a matter of this sort.
Later, when Guishan raised Huangbo’s question regarding the Wild Fox and asked Yangshan about it, Yangshan...
It is said that Huangbo constantly employed this device. Guishan asked, "Do you say it is obtained from Heaven, or obtained from others?
Yangshan replied, "It is both received through the lineage of the teacher and the realization of one's own school. Guishan said, "So it is, so it is."
Yuanwu asked, "How did the ancients of old bestow the Dharma upon others? The Master remained silent for a long while without speaking.
Yuanwu said, "What will you transmit to the descendants of future generations? The Master replied, "I thought you were a man of some substance. He then returned to his quarters.
While the Master was performing manual labor with Guishan, he asked, "Is there fire? Guishan replied, "There is. The Master asked, "Where is it?
Guishan took a stalk of firewood, blew on it, and handed it to the Master. The Master took it and said, "It is like insects eating wood."
While they were collectively clearing the land with hoes, a monk heard the sound of the drum, raised his hoe, and went back laughing.
The Master said, "How excellent! This is the gate through which Avalokiteśvara enters the principle. Later, he called the monk and asked, "What principle did you perceive today?
The monk replied, "This morning, before I had eaten my gruel, I heard the sound of the drum and went back to eat my meal. The Master then rebuked him.
He laughed heartily. He asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Who are you? He replied, "I am so-and-so. The Master said, "Do you recognize so-and-so?
He replied, "Clearly. The Master held up his whisk and asked, "Do you see the whisk? He replied, "I see it. Thereupon, the Master...
He did not speak.
The Master sent the monk to Changjing’s place, saying: "When you see him ascend the hall to preach the Dharma, you should immediately spread out your sitting mat and prostrate.
Then, picking up one of his shoes, brush away the dust on top with your sleeve and turn it upside down to cover [the other shoe]. That monk arrived at Changjing’s.
Respectfully. First, according to the Master’s intent, Zhangjing said, "This old monk is at fault.
While Guishan, Wufeng, and Yunyan were standing in attendance, the Master asked Guishan, "Seal off your throat, lips, and mouth, and speak quickly!
Guishan said, "I cannot say it; I beg the Master to speak for me. The Master said, "I do not decline to speak toward you..."
“Speak! I fear that later on you will cause me to lose my descendants. He then asked Wufeng. Wufeng said, “The Master must also close them up together.
The Master said, “In a place where there is no one, I shall rub my forehead and gaze at you. He then asked Yunyan. Yunyan said, “If I have attained the Way, please let the Master demonstrate it.
The Master said, “Close up your throat, lips, and mouth, and quickly speak what you have! Yunyan said, “Master—”
"Is there anyone here now? The Master said.
He ascended the hall and addressed the assembly, saying, "I need one person to go and deliver a message to the Abbot of Xitang. Who can go?"
Wufeng said, "I am capable of going. The Master asked, "How will you deliver the message? Wufeng said, "I will speak it once I have seen Xitang.
The Master asked, "What will you say after you see him? Wufeng said, "I will come back and report it to you, Master."
A monk asked Xitang, "Setting aside for a moment the case where there is a question and an answer, what is it like when there is neither question nor answer?
Tang said, "I am afraid it would rot away. When the Master heard this being cited, he said, "From the beginning, I have had doubts about this old fellow.
[The monk] said, "Please, Master, speak. The Master said, "A unified totality (ekaghanatva) cannot be apprehended."

The Master said to the assembly, "There is one person who has never eaten a meal in their life, yet they do not say they are hungry. There is another person who eats all day long, yet they do not say they are full. The assembly was speechless.
Yunyan asked, "Master, for whom do you labor so busily every day? The Master said, "There is one person who needs it.
Yunyan said, "Why do you not let him do it himself? The Master said, "He has no means of livelihood."
When the Master was a child, he accompanied his mother to a temple to pay homage to the Buddha. Pointing to the honored image, he asked his mother, "What is this?
His mother replied, "This is the Buddha. The child said, "His appearance is no different from that of a human being; I shall become one like him in the future as well."

The Master would always take the lead in manual labor and assume the most arduous tasks before the assembly. The community could not bear this and would hasten to gather their tools and request that he rest.
The Master would say, "I have no virtue; how could I compete with others for the labor? When the Master had searched everywhere for the tools and found none, [the assembly would insist].
He even forgot to eat; thus, the saying "if one does not work for a day, one does not eat for a day" spread throughout the world.
The Master entered nirvana on the seventeenth day of the first month in the ninth year of the Yuanhe era of the Tang dynasty, at the age of ninety-five.
In the first year of the Changqing era, an imperial edict conferred the posthumous title of Chan Master Dazhi. His stupa was named Dasheng Baolun.
This is the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dazhi of Baizhang Mountain in Hongzhou.
